scope: Major public development benchmark families, not an exhaustive ranking of all benchmarks. See task-inventory.json for exact indexed splits and task-examples.json for source-reviewed design cards. No leaderboard-score comparability is implied.

benchmarks.name: Datacurve DeepSWE
design_principles: Original tasks from real repositories
Behavioral verification that permits different implementations
Hold reference solutions and tests outside agent environments
benchmarks.application: Use fresh multi-step customer workflows with state, compatibility, and regression checks. Grade final observable behavior.
benchmarks.licensing: Reference links and methodology only. Check the license of each task and underlying repository before importing.
benchmarks.distinction: This is Datacurve’s benchmark, distinct from the Agentica/Together DeepSWE-Preview coding model. Customer runs here use native product harnesses, so are not comparable to its mini-swe-agent leaderboard.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench
design_principles: Pinned starting repository state
Reproducible container environment
Fail-to-pass behavior and pass-to-pass regression checks
benchmarks.application: Turn a workflow into a specific issue with a failing behavioral check, plus regression tests. Preserve the base commit and dependencies.
benchmarks.licensing: No dataset bundled. Imported code and benchmark material require their respective licenses.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench / Harbor task format
design_principles: Self-contained task environment
Explicit instruction and resource/time limits
Executable verifier and held-out oracle
benchmarks.application: Validate tangible filesystem or program outputs in a clean verifier environment. Pin toolchain and avoid external service dependencies.
benchmarks.licensing: No task files copied. Review each upstream task and dependency license before reuse.

benchmarks.name: Aider Polyglot
design_principles: Executable coding exercises across languages
Report editing correctness and cost
Document retry protocol
benchmarks.application: Useful inspiration for small/medium coding tasks with explicit language/runtime constraints. This runner uses one attempt per repeat, without automated repair retries.
benchmarks.licensing: Original examples only. Exercise collections have separate upstream licenses.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Pro
design_principles: Reconstruct the issue contract and pair fail-to-pass with regression checks. Review requirements and verifiers independently; historical tests are not automatically sufficient.
benchmarks.application: Reconstruct the issue contract and pair fail-to-pass with regression checks. Review requirements and verifiers independently; historical tests are not automatically sufficient.
benchmarks.licensing: Original summaries and source metadata only. Inspect each upstream license before copying task code, tests, assets, or datasets.

benchmarks.name: SWE-Lancer implementation tasks
design_principles: Replay user interactions in an isolated app and inspect observable outcomes. Managerial proposal-selection tasks are excluded from the coding-task inventory.
benchmarks.application: Replay user interactions in an isolated app and inspect observable outcomes. Managerial proposal-selection tasks are excluded from the coding-task inventory.
benchmarks.licensing: Original summaries and source metadata only. Inspect each upstream license before copying task code, tests, assets, or datasets.
